strengths: Novel application of information geometry to analyze softmax parameterization, with formal theoretical results showing diagonal FIM structure
Technically sound mathematical proofs (Propositions 4.1, Theorem 4.2, Corollary 4.3) with detailed appendices
Comprehensive experimental validation across three diverse domains (GSL, VAE, RL) with consistent improvements
Excellent reproducibility with detailed experimental protocols, public datasets, and clear hyperparameter search descriptions
Clear presentation with good intuition for hierarchical binary structure
weaknesses: Critical gap between theory and practice: diagonal FIM advantage is not leveraged since natural gradient descent is not implemented; standard optimizers (Adam) don't directly use FIM
Empirical improvements are modest and often within experimental variance: GSL improvements are small, VAE gains are 0.3-1.5 NLL, and RL gains overlap with error bars (Seaquest: 2164±533 vs 1875±312)
Unfair parameter comparison: catnat uses O(K log K) parameters vs O(K) for softmax; this capacity difference is not adequately controlled or analyzed

Missing critical comparisons with recent gradient estimation techniques (REBAR, RELAX, REINFORCE with baselines); Gumbel-Softmax and other discrete VAE methods not compared as standalone parameterizations
Binary tree structure is inefficient for non-power-of-2 cardinalities, requires log_2(K) depth causing potential gradient flow issues, and scalability for large K is not analyzed
Limited ablation studies: marginal differences between catnat-σ and catnat-ν raise questions about the value of the complex natural activation function
Different gradient estimators across experiments (Score Function, Gumbel-Softmax, PPO) confound results; unclear whether improvements stem from parameterization or estimator choice
RL results lack statistical significance: paper acknowledges 'high variance' and overlapping confidence intervals, yet treats results as conclusive evidence

strengths: Novel information-geometric perspective on softmax parameterization with rigorous theoretical analysis proving diagonal Fisher Information Matrix for catnat
Comprehensive experimental validation across three diverse domains (GSL, VAE, RL) with consistent improvements and excellent reproducibility
Practical implementation with code provided in PyTorch and JAX, compatible with standard training methods
Mathematically rigorous proofs (Theorem 4.2) with careful analysis of hierarchical tree structure properties
Thorough experimental documentation with statistical significance testing and multiple random seeds across different optimizers
weaknesses: Modest effect sizes (1-5% improvements) with overlapping error bars suggest limited practical significance relative to added complexity
Theory-practice gap: diagonal FIM proven for intermediate scores but connection to actual optimization improvements and global parameter-space FIM remains unclear and informal

Source of improvements not convincingly isolated between hierarchical structure itself and engineered natural activation function ν; catnat-σ often underperforms catnat-ν suggesting activation function carries significant weight
Limited reinforcement learning evaluation (only 2 Atari environments) with acknowledged incomplete hyperparameter search due to computational constraints
No investigation of scalability to very large K or behavior outside tested regimes (3-class examples in Figure 1); missing comparison with other information-geometry-inspired optimization methods
Significant added complexity (hierarchical tree with O(log K) binary decisions and custom activation) compared to softmax simplicity may limit practical adoption
